The Trust aims to encourage new approaches that may establish or reshape a field of study.
The Trust aims to transform our understanding of a significant contemporary topic.
Applicants are invited to be bold in their bids.
Centres should have the capacity to become internationally recognised for excellence.
The Trust encourages higher-risk, fundamental, curiosity-driven ('blue skies'), and multi-disciplinary research.
Centres are expected to draw upon a range of disciplinary perspectives and expertise.
The choice of research topic is open, but medical and clinical research are ineligible.
The chosen topic should be large-scale enough to support an ambitious research agenda for up to ten years.
Leverhulme Research Centres should not duplicate existing activity at a comparable scale.
The Trust wishes to support research where it can be confident of substantial added value.
Funding requested should be proportionate to the centre’s proposed duration.
Research centres will be encouraged to seek additional concurrent support from other funding bodies.
The Trust will not award follow-on funding.
At least 75% of resources must fund research staff (research assistants, postgraduate students, replacement teaching).
Replacement teaching is funded at a maximum of 33% for up to three years for key academic staff.
Associated research costs (technical, computing, administrative staff, travel, dissemination, consumables) can be up to 25% of the total budget.
Institutions hosting a centre must provide office and workspace and other university support.
The Trust does not fund 'infrastructural' investment or overheads.
The Trust does not make awards on a full economic costing basis.
Increases in costs over the lifetime of centres must be managed within the awarded funding.
Prospective applicants should follow their university’s internal selection process first.

Process and closing dates for later stages will be notified to shortlisted applicants.

Applications must be submitted by a principal applicant based in a UK university who will act as Director.
Details of the proposed wider leadership team should be provided.
Applications are considered via a two-stage process: outline bid and detailed proposal.
The outline bid includes a short form and a five-page description of the centre's structure and research activity.
The description should include the research area, key research questions, and how the centre will contribute.
The description should detail the centre's structure, including single or multi-site, institutions involved, and key staff.
The description should justify the choice of principal applicant and senior staff.
The description should indicate how resources might be used over the centre’s duration.
Outline bids will be shortlisted, and successful applicants invited to submit a detailed proposal.
A statement of support from the applying institution is required for the detailed proposal.
Full applications that are shortlisted will lead to an invitation for an interview.
Final decisions are anticipated to be made by the Trust Board at a subsequent board meeting.
The Trust is unable to provide feedback on applications.
